::: {#exr-one-hot-product}

#### Multiplying a one-hot vector by a matrix

A network that reads text needs each character as a vector.
Number the 26 lowercase letters and the space from 0 to 26,
so `"c"` is 2.
Let $\vecf{e}_2 \in \{0, 1\}^{27}$ be the [one-hot encoding](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/big-ideas.html#def-one-hot-encoding) of `"c"`,
and let $\matr{E}$ be the $27 \times 4$ matrix printed below.
What is $\tp{\vecf{e}_2} \matr{E}$?

```{python}
#| code-fold: show
alphabet = "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz "
_ = torch.manual_seed(2)
E = torch.randn(len(alphabet), 4).round(decimals=2)
print(E[:4])
```

:::
